prize_parts.citation: For the development of dye-sensitized nanocrystalline solar cells, in which a mesoporous molecular-sensitised oxide film separates light absorption from charge transport.

statement.case_for: The 1991 O'Regan and Grätzel cell is a clean case of architecture determining function: a mesoporous nanocrystalline TiO2 film with a molecular sensitiser separates light absorption from charge collection. It is original, was confirmed by many independent groups over more than three decades, founded molecular and hybrid photovoltaics, and is the conceptual ancestor of the later perovskite cells. Credit is unusually clear for a two-person prize: the 1991 Nature paper is the decisive contribution and Grätzel drove the field. Among the shortlisted candidates it combines mature validation, a sharp discovery and a short, defensible laureate list, and it is the only one whose recognition would be clearly overdue rather than merely timely.
statement.case_against: Dye-sensitised cells never achieved the commercial efficiency or market share once expected, and perovskites have overtaken them, so a critic can say the practical impact is smaller than the scientific influence. The prize would also leave out Hagfeldt, who made major later contributions to mechanism and devices, and the committee may prefer a discovery with more visible biomedical consequences, such as targeted protein degradation, which has stronger first-place support in the opening ballots.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B011) is a new drug modality built on molecular design, turning previously undruggable proteins into removable targets, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the core.
responses.response: I agree the concept is original and that B011 deserves the strong opening support it received. My reservation is attribution and maturity rather than merit. The molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) is a distinct lineage that a three-name cap cannot honour fairly, and no degrader is yet an approved drug, so the claimed clinical consequence is still a promise. I would put B011 as my first alternative and would support it if the citation is kept to the rational bifunctional degrader concept and the committee accepts that clinical validation is still maturing.

responses.point: Long-range electron transfer through proteins (B058, Gray and Winkler) gives the physical framework for biological electron transfer, and nitrogenase (B008) is a well-defined mechanistic problem in metalloenzyme chemistry.
responses.response: I respect the B058 rigour and agree the two-name credit is clean. But the field overlaps with Marcus theory, already recognised in 1992, and with the Moser and Dutton and Beratan and Onuchic work, so the claim needs a narrow definition that the supplied credit does not give. For B008 I am more sympathetic. The FeMo-cofactor structures are real structural achievements, but as you note, the binding of N2 and the full catalytic mechanism remain open, and with Dean, Ribbe, Rees, Einsle and Seefeldt all credible, the three-name cap forces a contestable cut. I keep it as an alternative, not as my preference.

responses.point: The dye-sensitised cell (B005) separates absorption from transport through a mesoporous film, is a clear physical-chemical design principle, and Hagfeldt is a later contributor rather than a founding name. Linke himself ranks nanopore sequencing (B017) first.
responses.response: We agree on B005 and on the two-name attribution, and I appreciate that you also treat the efficiency plateau as not weakening the scientific case. On B017 I see a real tool, but credit is the problem: Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Akeson and Bayley each hold a different step, from translocation to pore engineering to enzyme ratcheting, and a three-name split leaves out people who made decisive contributions. I would want that attribution settled before ranking it above a candidate with a clean two-person credit.

responses.point: Biomolecular phase separation (B035) is a new organising principle of the cell, reducing cell biology to multivalency and phase behaviour, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen as the core.
responses.response: I see the conceptual appeal, but I would qualify it on structural evidence. The existence of liquid-like condensates is well shown, but their biological generality and functional role are still debated, and the structural basis of the interactions is often disordered and hard to define. As a structural chemist I want to know that the mechanism was actually established, not only that droplets form in vitro. I am less ready to rank it with a discovery whose structure-function relationship is demonstrated and widely reproduced.

responses.point: Palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (B055) is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis and Buchwald and Hartwig are the decisive contributors, with Kosugi as an antecedent.
responses.response: I agree that B055 has the strongest adoption record and a clean credit story, and it is a serious competitor to my preference. Where we differ is the novelty margin: the 2010 coupling prize already honours the Pd cross-coupling concept, so the committee may see C-N coupling as an extension of a recognised principle. Dye-sensitised cells open a different field. I do not consider this settled, and I would not oppose B055 if the committee judges the extension worthy.

uncertainties: Whether the committee would require Hagfeldt to be included, which would make three names for B005.
Whether the committee will read the later dominance of perovskite cells as lowering the practical impact of the dye-sensitised work.
Whether the molecular-glue strand of B011 can be separated cleanly from PROTACs in a citation.
I cannot independently verify the precise credit split in the supplied B008 and B011 lists.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the proposed laureates. My only listed connection is a Stockholm University colleague relationship with Peter Brzezinski, which does not bear on B005.
